description: The review panel of docs/PROJECT.md §3, and nothing else. The panel reads the transcript it was handed, shows it, and answers with transfer / copy / cancel / re-record / re-clean — all of which are commands this application defines itself in src/panel.rs and which therefore need no entry here. It opens no dialogs, runs no shell commands, and reaches no network: audio and text never leave the machine, and a webview that could open a socket would make that claim unverifiable. WP3 registers tauri-plugin-dialog for the model-download consent question and deliberately grants the panel NONE of its permissions: that dialog is asked from Rust, on the engine's own thread, about the machine rather than about the panel — and a webview that could raise a native dialog could also raise one that looks like this application asking a question it never asked. Two permissions beyond the core defaults, each for one gesture: core:window:allow-hide, because the panel hides itself on Esc and after a transfer; and core:window:allow-start-dragging (added in WP5b), because the card is draggable and a drag has to begin inside the webview, where the mouse-down happens — it moves the window the user is already holding and cannot aim it at anything on its own, which is why it is granted where allow-set-position is not. Specifically NOT granted: allow-show, allow-set-position, allow-set-size and allow-set-focus. The panel is created, placed, resized and focused by the Rust side, which owns the non-activating window style (focusable: false, i.e. WS_EX_NOACTIVATE) that keeps the focus in the application the user is dictating into. A webview that could show, move, resize or focus its own window could undo that, and the target window losing focus is the one failure this design exists to prevent — so the height the text needs is measured in the page and applied through the panel_resize command, which clamps it.
